title: Dynamic Globe, Shell, and Magnetic Overlay
objective: Make the two-layer root visible and debuggable via a deterministic, serializable rendering-contract spec (no DOM/canvas): build_overlay_state(epoch, shell) yields the layers a globe view would draw.

repository_truth.head: de620bb
reused_engine: cwatlas.r1082.root_certificate.resolve (cached fixed+dynamic root) + southup (viewpoint-safe handedness); wilkes / saa via the certificate - NOT reimplemented

implementation.viewpoint_safe_arrows: clockwise-positive from the Antarctic external viewpoint; anticlockwise from the North-down inverse view (same physical rotation)
implementation.browser_ui: OUT_OF_SCOPE_SPEC_LEVEL_ONLY - node exists but the browser UI is untestable in this environment

claims.statement: build_overlay_state(epoch, shell) generates the serializable layered state of the locked two-layer root - a fixed epoch-independent Wilkes root marker, a dynamic SAA phase-zero direction at (epoch, shell), a South-Up orientation frame with viewpoint-safe arrows, the shell radius, and candidate pins/regions.

negative_results: The FIXED Wilkes root marker is epoch-independent: animating the epoch never rotates it (verified across an epoch series); only the DYNAMIC SAA layer moves with epoch and shell.
Out of field-model validity the overlay returns a typed MODEL_VALIDITY_REFUSAL layer, never an invented direction.

The overlay renders no pixels, measures nothing, and asserts no physical effect; candidate pins are software results under a declared calibration (CALIBRATED_CANDIDATE at most), validating no source origin.
privacy_check: CLEAN - synthetic/public epochs, shells, and candidate outputs only; no private path literals, no personal identity tokens, no raw private narrative
